chunks: And from him (Al-Hasan ibn al-Walid) from Al-Nadr from Hisham from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the two rak'ahs before Fajr prayer. He said: 'Perform them when you leave the Gada (early morning) prayer, for they are before the Gada.'

key_terms.الْغَدَاةَ: The Gada (early morning) prayer, referring to the Fajr prayer

ai.seo_question: When should the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr be performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the timing of the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr, specifying that they are performed after the obligatory Fajr prayer but are legally categorized as 'before' it (Qabl al-Ghada) because they precede the rising of the sun (Shuruq). This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance where the temporal sequence of performance differs from the legal classification of the prayer relative to the sun's position.
